analysis.title: The Point for Europe, Wednesday, 11 November 2026
key_insights: Top Call: Nike (NKE) hosts a capital markets day on 16-17 Nov. Citi expects NKE to confirm its strategy for sportswear, Jordan and Greater China, the three areas management flagged for improvement at 1Q27 results. Sportswear and Jordan were a high-single-digit drag on NKE consolidated sales growth in that quarter.

Citi assumes a positive read-across to JD Sports if NKE shows a strong product pipeline, particularly in Lifestyle/Footwear, and stresses premium Wholesale distribution. For Adidas and Puma, the market is expected to focus on NKE's China strategy and global product pipeline.

Sneaker resale tracker (StockX data): total resale volumes fell -0.8% MoM in October, the 12th consecutive monthly decline. Excluding NKE (-0.2% MoM), the market fell -2.2% MoM. Adidas lost 25bps of resale share, Puma lost 2bps and NKE gained 39bps, its 8th straight monthly gain. Next catalysts are NKE's CMD on 16-17 Nov and JD Sports' 3Q27 trading update on 19 Nov.
Marks & Spencer held its 2026 Capital Markets Day, focused on the margin opportunity in Fashion, Home & Beauty. Citi lists five takeaways, but the excerpt does not give the details.

DSV: Citi's 4Q26E adjusted operating profit of DKK7,064m is c.4% above Bloomberg consensus, mainly in Air and Sea. Its GP/TEU forecast of DKK4,183 is c.4% above consensus and Air GP/ton of DKK9,218 is c.5% above. Air and Sea GP of DKK9,721m compares with consensus of DKK9,229m. Air freight rate indices point to a strong peak season, and Sept/Oct container rates sit above June-August levels.

GSK: Citi trims near-term EPS by 1% and cuts its target price to £20.50 from £21.00, staying Neutral. Reasons are the slowest 27-30E EPS CAGR in the sector (3%), few 2027 catalysts, and overhangs from the Apretude Q4M filing and the AnaptysBio Jemperli litigation outcome (4Q26/1Q27). The stock trades at about 10x 27E P/E.

Infineon: F4Q results support the view that it is more than a cyclical recovery story. Datacentre visibility is improving through raised FY27 guidance (c€4bn datacentre revenue) and capacity reservation agreements above €10bn. Citi calls the recent pullback an attractive entry point at c.12x FY28E P/E, while investors worry about datacentre deployment delays.

Atlas Copco (Buy reiterated): shares have underperformed the SXNP by 10% since the mid-October peak, after outperforming by 26% over the prior 12 months. Citi says a sustained semis recovery is no longer priced in on its base-case WFE forecast. It sees upside to the VT (Vacuum Technique) Street margin on pricing, and a possible near-term slowdown in 4Q VT orders. Target price is cut to SKr249 from SKr259.

Rheinmetall: 2030 Bloomberg consensus (€38bn sales, €7.7bn EBIT) is about 16% below company guidance (€45bn sales, over €9bn EBIT). Citi estimates the share price discounts a further 34-48% cut to consensus. The company CMD is on 27 Nov. Citi sets out three scenarios: guidance cut with a reset (shares up if the cut is under 50%), no cut and no credibility (shares drift sideways), or no cut with credibility restored (positive but unlikely).

DSM-Firmenich: at a London roadshow the CEO expressed confidence in the 2027 outlook for growth and margins, with no material change expected in current trends. Management expects a 21% EBITDA margin even under a similar FX headwind. DSM is the only HMO producer with its own manufacturing facility and should face effectively no competition in China for possibly another year. North American consumer demand remains soft, and a normalisation would add upside.

Hensoldt: the CMD addressed whether growth plateaus after 2030. 63% of last year's sales were to Germany, whose defense budget is expected to rise from ~2% in 2024 to 3.5% in 2029/30. Post-2030 growth comes from exports and services and training revenue (16% of sales in 2025 to 25% in 2035). The 2035 ambition of €9bn organic sales implies ~10% CAGR 2030-35, which matches Citi's target price.

Air France-KLM: Citi raises FY26/FY27 operating profit to €2.0bn from €1.4bn/€1.8bn after 3Q26 results and lifts its target price to €14.6, implying 3% upside, staying Neutral. Non-fuel unit cost growth fell to +0.5% from +4%. Citi's medium-term margin is c6.5% against the company's target of over 8%. If the momentum continues, it would estimate fair value at €30.4.

Freenet and Telefonica signed a term sheet for a new ten-year partnership, suggesting an end to their dispute. It is not a final contract and no financial terms were given. It may help offset part of the c€50m a year headwind disclosed in February. Freenet reports Q3 tomorrow post-close and Telefonica reports Thursday morning.

European airline positioning: airlines remain consensus short after results, though positioning turned more bullish. Air France-KLM moved into the consensus long quadrant, IAG strengthened, and Lufthansa improved. Wizz still has the highest short positioning. Ryanair remains a two-way debate.

European aerospace and defense crowding: aerospace is a two-way debate with improving positioning, and Rolls-Royce is back in consensus long. Defense remains consensus long, but positioning weakened over the week. Rheinmetall saw a sharp fall in longs and rebuilt shorts after results. Hensoldt is nearing consensus long, and Dassault and Babcock moved to consensus short.

UK grocery (Worldpanel, P11 to 1-Nov): till roll sales +2.2% and food inflation +2.6%. Tesco (+1.8%) and Sainsbury's (+1.0%) lagged the market and lost share. Morrisons grew +2.4%, Asda was -0.2% and M&S grocery was +15.1%. Citi expects some weakness in Tesco shares today.

Spain banks: in 3Q26 SAN and BBVA gained deposit share YoY, partly from wholesale and public sector deposits, which also raised deposit costs. SAN, BBVA and CABK gained lending share. Citi prefers BBVA (Buy) on expected strong Mexico volume growth in 2027E.

Luxury pricing tracker: October price increases were limited. Balenciaga raised prices by about 6% on about 15% of its SKUs and Pandora by about 9% on about 15% of its assortment. Citi expects pricing to keep normalising and says it is unlikely to offset weaker volumes, but should support low-to-mid-single-digit cFX sector sales growth in FY27-28E.

Citi's quantitative regime model stays in the 'Normal' expansion cluster but tilts late-cycle on tighter financial conditions and rising volatility. Equities move to neutral with the US the largest underweight, and duration stays overweight via JGBs and Gilts. IG credit keeps a maximum underweight while HY moves overweight. Energy stays overweight and base metals flips short. Historical analogues have shifted toward the late-1970s pre-Volcker backdrop.

Rating and target changes: Ferguson (Buy) TP to US$303 from US$288, Commerzbank (Neutral) TP to €40 from €42, Air France-KLM (Neutral/High risk) TP to €14.60 from €12.20, GSK (Neutral) TP to £20.50 from £21.00, Atlas Copco (Buy) TP to SKr249 from SKr259.

market_movers.rationale: Target price raised to US$303 from US$288 with Buy unchanged. Closing price was US$259.44. The excerpt gives no reasoning.
Commerzbank target price cut to €40 from €42 with Neutral unchanged. Closing price was €40.17. The excerpt gives no reasoning.
Air France-KLM target price raised to €14.6 from €12.20 after FY26/FY27 operating profit estimates rose to €2.0bn. Citi stays Neutral and sees €30.4 fair value if underlying momentum persists.
Target price trimmed to £20.50 from £21.00 and near-term EPS cut 1% on lower sales and higher pipeline investment. Neutral stays on slow EPS growth and few catalysts.
Atlas Copco target price cut to SKr249 from SKr259 with Buy reiterated. Citi says a semis recovery is no longer priced in after the de-rating.
Rheinmetall carries an upside 30-day Catalyst Watch into the 27 Nov CMD. Citi thinks the share price discounts 34-48% further cuts to consensus.
Citi prefers BBVA among Spanish banks on expected strong volume growth in Mexico in 2027E.
Infineon: Citi calls the recent share price pullback an attractive entry point at c.12x FY28E P/E. No rating or target is stated in the excerpt.
Hensoldt: the 2035 ambition of €9bn organic sales implies ~10% CAGR 2030-35, which Citi says matches its target price. No rating is stated in the excerpt.
DSV: Citi's 4Q26E adjusted operating profit is c.4% above consensus, supporting upgrades to estimates.

sector_views.rationale: Defense positioning remains consensus long despite Rheinmetall weakness, and aerospace is a two-way debate with improving positioning.
Airlines remain consensus short after results, with positioning turning more bullish. Investors debate next summer's fare strength after capacity cuts.
Pricing is normalising and is unlikely to offset weaker volumes, though it should support low-to-mid-single-digit cFX sales growth in FY27-28E.
Sneaker resale volumes keep declining while NKE outperforms. NKE's CMD is the next catalyst for the sector.
Deposit and lending share gains at SAN, BBVA and CABK. Citi prefers BBVA on Mexico volume growth.

earnings_insights: DSV 4Q26E (Citi estimate, not yet reported): adjusted operating profit DKK7,064m, c.4% above Bloomberg consensus. GP/TEU DKK4,183 is c.4% above consensus and Air GP/ton DKK9,218 is c.5% above. Air and Sea GP is DKK9,721m against Bloomberg consensus of DKK9,229m.
Infineon F4Q results (already reported): FY27 guidance raised to c€4bn datacentre revenue, with signed capacity reservation agreements above €10bn and a strong Q4 exit run-rate.

Air France-KLM (3Q26 results reported last week): Citi estimates FY26 operating profit of €2.0bn against €1.4bn prior and FY27 of €2.0bn against €1.8bn prior. Non-fuel unit cost growth was +0.5% against +4% a year earlier.

GSK: Citi trims near-term EPS estimates by 1% on slightly lower 2026E sales (Fx/Dovato ex-US LOE) and lower 2027E/2028E margins. It sees 22 Phase III trial starts in 2026E that annualize in 2027E. Citi's 27-30E EPS CAGR for GSK is 3%.
Freenet reports Q3 results tomorrow post-close (call Thursday 11am CET) and Telefonica reports Q3 on Thursday morning (call 10am CET). Citi expects the Telefonica term sheet to feature in both.

UK grocery: Worldpanel P11 (4 weeks to 1 Nov, already published) till roll sales +2.2%, Tesco +1.8%, Sainsbury's +1.0%. Nielsen 12-week data to 31 Oct suggests Tesco market share +10bps YoY, and Citi assumes Nielsen 12-week Tesco sales of +2.6% against Worldpanel 12-week +1.2%.
Atlas Copco: Citi's ex-VT/semis organic sales CAGR is likely 6% through to 2030. It sees Street CT margin for 2027 as too high and sees upside to the VT Street margin.

macro_indicators.indicator: Sneaker resale volumes, all brands (StockX proxy)
macro_indicators.interpretation: 12th straight monthly decline, after -0.5% on the prior 3-month average. Excluding NKE the market fell -2.2% MoM.
Citi expects it to stay at 3.5% afterwards, which supports Hensoldt's growth through 2030.

trade_ideas.description: Long Rheinmetall via Citi's 30-day Catalyst Watch (upside) into the 27 Nov capital markets day
trade_ideas.rationale: Shares price in 34-48% further cuts to consensus, so a guidance reset of under 50% would lift them.
trade_ideas.risk: If the company neither cuts guidance nor rebuilds credibility, shares drift sideways.

trade_ideas.description: Long BBVA (Citi's preferred Spanish bank, Buy)
trade_ideas.rationale: Citi expects strong volume growth in Mexico in 2027E.

risk_factors: Possible datacentre deployment delays weigh on sentiment toward Infineon.
Rheinmetall has lost market credibility and may fail to reset targets at its 27 Nov CMD.
A near-term slowdown in 4Q VT orders at Atlas Copco.
GSK overhangs: uncertainty over the EXTEND4M Apretude Q4M filing and the AnaptysBio Jemperli litigation outcome in 4Q26/1Q27.
Tighter financial conditions or a growth rollover would move Citi's regime model to a less constructive regime.
Weaker volumes in luxury as pressure on aspirational consumers limits pricing power.
Soft North American consumer demand for DSM-Firmenich.
The Freenet and Telefonica term sheet is not a finalised contract and carries no disclosed financial terms.
vol_and_positioning: European airlines remain consensus short post results, with positioning more bullish w/w and m/m. Air France-KLM moved into consensus long, IAG strengthened, Lufthansa improved clearly, and Wizz has the highest short positioning. Ryanair is a two-way debate with small cuts to both longs and shorts.

European aerospace is a two-way debate with improved positioning. Rolls-Royce moved back to consensus long, and Airbus and Safran are highly crowded on both sides. MTU and Melrose have elevated shorts.

Defense remains consensus long but weakened over the week. Rheinmetall saw a sharp fall in longs and a rebuild in shorts after results. Hensoldt is approaching consensus long and Renk was little changed. BAE, SAAB, Leonardo and Thales keep strong long positioning, while Dassault and Babcock moved to consensus short and QinetiQ is in investor apathy.

Citi's regime model notes rising volatility and tighter financial conditions tilting it late-cycle. Systematic strategies are positive year-to-date, with carry and a modest value uptick offsetting trend-following losses.
geopolitical: German defense spending is expected to rise to 3.5% of GDP by 2029/30, underpinning European defense companies such as Hensoldt and Rheinmetall.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus is already about 16% below guidance and the share price implies a further 34-48% of cuts. A guidance reset of under 50% in total would lift the shares.
tension_points.bear_case: Rheinmetall appears to have lost market credibility. If it keeps guidance without rebuilding credibility, shares drift sideways.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A guidance cut at the 27 Nov CMD larger than 50% in total (the 16% consensus gap plus Citi's 34% estimate).

tension_points.bull_case: After the de-rating, a sustained semis recovery is not priced in on Citi's base-case WFE forecast. Service and OE growth in CT and VT pricing offer upside.
tension_points.bear_case: 4Q orders in VT could slow near term and CT Street margin for 2027 still looks too high.

tension_points.bull_case: Non-fuel unit cost growth fell to +0.5% from +4%. If it persists, medium-term margin ambitions look achievable and fair value would be €30.4.
tension_points.bear_case: Citi's medium-term margin of c6.5% is below the company target of over 8%, and the target price of €14.6 implies only 3% upside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Underlying momentum failing to persist, such as non-fuel unit cost growth rising back toward last year's +4%.
